pairs.supplier_statement_or_definition: Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open with $n\ge1$ and $\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$. Then $C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ is dense in $L^2(\Omega;\mathbb K)$: for every $f\in L^2(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ and every $\delta>0$ there is $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ with $\|\varphi-f\|_{L^2(\Omega)}<\delta$. pairs.actual_fact_text: [[lem-na-polynomial-coefficient-bound-from-fixed-nodes]]: on any fixed $n+1$ distinct nodes, each polynomial coefficient is a fixed linear combination of the sampled values.
pairs.supplier_statement_or_definition:
Let $n\ge0$ and let $t_0,\ldots,t_n$ be distinct real numbers. For
$0\le j\le n$, define
$$L_j(x):=\prod_{k\ne j}\frac{x-t_k}{t_j-t_k}.$$
If $p(x)=\sum_{k=0}^{n}c_kx^k$ has degree at most $n$, then
$$p(x)=\sum_{j=0}^{n}p(t_j)L_j(x).$$
Consequently, writing $L_j(x)=\sum_{k=0}^{n}\ell_{jk}x^k$, every coefficient
satisfies
$$|c_k|\le\left(\sum_{j=0}^{n}|\ell_{jk}|\right)\max_{0\le j\le n}|p(t_j)|.$$
The empty product convention gives $L_0=1$ when $n=0$.
pairs.classification: nonnegative integer degree explicitly supplied by current Statement and Given
pairs.mathematical_reason: The consumer Statement and Given explicitly fix an integer n>=0. Proof1.1 writes p_c=sum_{j=0}^n c_j x^j. Proof2.1 separately handles n=0 with the single node a, and for n>=1 chooses n+1 distinct real nodes a+j(b-a)/n in the nondegenerate interval. This is exactly the source degree-at-most-n Lagrange representation. The fact is a scoped assertion about those polynomials, not all polynomials of unrestricted degree.

pairs.actual_fact_text: [[thm-exponential-is-strictly-increasing]], [[cor-exponential-reciprocal-and-positivity]], [[def-continuity-and-derivative-on-real-interval]], [[thm-derivative-of-exponential]], [[lem-derivative-algebra-and-chain-rules]], and [[def-real-elementary-functions-and-domains]]: $\exp$ is continuous and strictly increasing, $\exp(0)=1$ by its power series, and $\exp(x)>0$ for every real $x$; the difference-quotient definition and scalar power, sum and chain rules show each summand $x\mapsto\exp(-\alpha(x+n)^2)$ is differentiable and hence continuous, so each finite partial sum is continuous.
pairs.supplier_statement_or_definition:
Every integral below is the oriented Riemann integral constructed from upper
and lower Darboux sums in
[[lem-continuous-functions-riemann-integrable]]. It exists for each displayed
continuous integrand on the finite interval between its endpoints, is additive
in intervals, reverses sign when the endpoints are reversed, is monotone in
the integrand, and satisfies
$|\int_a^b g(t)\,dt|\le|b-a|\max_{t\text{ between }a\text{ and }b}|g(t)|$.
These properties also
give constant comparison bounds and the average-value difference quotient
used to differentiate the integral-defined functions.

The exponential is $\exp(x)=\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}x^k/k!$ for $x\in\mathbb R$.
The sine and cosine are the everywhere-convergent power series
$\sin x=\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}(-1)^k x^{2k+1}/(2k+1)!$ and
$\cos x=\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}(-1)^k x^{2k}/(2k)!$. Define
$\arctan x=\int_0^x dt/(1+t^2)$ and set $\pi=4\arctan1$. The natural
logarithm $\ln$ is defined on $(0,\infty)$ by $\ln x=\int_1^x dt/t$.

The square root is the unique nonnegative real $y$ with $y^2=x$ for $x\ge0$;
existence and uniqueness follow from
[[lem-nonnegative-square-root-exists-and-unique]]. The tangent is
$\tan x=\sin x/\cos x$ on the set where $\cos x\ne0$.

For complex $z=x+iy$, the modulus $|z|=\sqrt{x^2+y^2}$ is defined in
[[def-intervals-rectangles-and-complex-balls]]. The complex exponential is
$\exp(x+iy)=\exp(x)(\cos y+i\sin y)$. The principal complex logarithm is
$\operatorname{Log}(z)=\ln|z|+i\operatorname{Arg}(z)$ on
$\mathbb C\setminus(-\infty,0]$. For $z=x+iy$ in this domain, define
$$\operatorname{Arg}(x+iy)= \begin{cases} \arctan(y/x),&x>0,\\ \pi/2,&x=0,\ y>0,\\ -\pi/2,&x=0,\ y<0,\\ \pi-\arctan(y/(-x)),&x<0,\ y>0,\\ -\pi+\arctan((-y)/(-x)),&x<0,\ y<0. \end{cases}$$
The excluded negative real axis is the remaining case $x<0,y=0$; zero is
also excluded.

These are point functions. An interval extension must separately enclose their
exact ranges, test the stated domains, and return a non-finite status when its
finite budget cannot certify a reduction or endpoint.

pairs.actual_fact_text: For any open $\Omega$, zero extension maps $W_0^{1,p}(\Omega)$ isometrically into $W^{1,p}(\mathbb R^d)$, with weak gradient the zero extension of $\nabla v$ ([[lem-zero-extension-from-w-one-p-zero]]).
pairs.supplier_statement_or_definition:
Assume Countable Choice. For any open $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$,
$n\ge1$, any $1\le p\le\infty$ and any
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, extension by zero
$$E_0u(x)=u(x)\ \ (x\in\Omega),\qquad E_0u(x)=0\ \ (x\notin\Omega),$$
acted on representatives, sends $W_0^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ linearly into
$W^{1,p}(\mathbb R^n;\mathbb K)$. For every $u\in W_0^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$
and every coordinate direction $i$, the class $D_i(E_0u)$ is the zero
extension of the class $D_iu$, and every $L^p$ component norm is preserved:
$$\|E_0u\|_{L^p(\mathbb R^n)}=\|u\|_{L^p(\Omega)},\qquad \|D_i(E_0u)\|_{L^p(\mathbb R^n)}=\|D_iu\|_{L^p(\Omega)},$$
so that $\|E_0u\|_{W^{1,p}(\mathbb R^n)}=\|u\|_{W^{1,p}(\Omega)}$.

pairs.supplier_statement_or_definition:
Let $n \ge 1$ and **assume the Axiom of Countable Choice**
([[def-countable-choice]]). Then:

1. $\lambda_n$ is sigma-finite ([[def-finite-sigma-finite-and-semifinite-measures]]):
   the cubes $(-k,k]^n$ are Lebesgue measurable with
   $\lambda_n\big((-k,k]^n\big) = (2k)^n < +\infty$, they increase with $k$, and
   their union over $k \in \mathbb{N}$ is $\mathbb{R}^n$.
2. Every bounded subset $E \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$
   ([[def-metric-bounded-diameter]]) has $\lambda_n^*(E) < +\infty$; a bounded
   Lebesgue measurable set therefore has finite measure, and every compact
   subset of $\mathbb{R}^n$ is Lebesgue measurable of finite measure.

pairs.actual_fact_text: [[lem-pe18-spherical-harmonic-structure-and-density]]: $\Delta=\partial_{rr}+2r^{-1}\partial_r+r^{-2}\Delta_{\mathbb S^2}$, $\Delta_{\mathbb S^2}w_\ell=-\ell(\ell+1)w_\ell$, and $\|w_\ell\|_{C^p}\le C_p(1+\ell)^{p+1/2}\|w_\ell\|_2$ for every fixed $p$.
pairs.supplier_statement_or_definition:
Let $\mathcal H_\ell$ be the degree-$\ell$ spaces on $\mathbb S^2$ from [[def-three-dimensional-spherical-harmonic-space]], with surface measure of total mass $4\pi$, and let $P_\ell$ be orthogonal projection in $L^2(\mathbb S^2)$. Define $\Delta_{\mathbb S^2}$ by the polar-coordinate identity $\Delta=\partial_{rr}+2r^{-1}\partial_r+r^{-2}\Delta_{\mathbb S^2}$. Then $\Delta_{\mathbb S^2}g=-\ell(\ell+1)g$ for $g\in\mathcal H_\ell$; for all smooth $v,w$ on the sphere, $\langle v,\Delta_{\mathbb S^2}w\rangle=\langle\Delta_{\mathbb S^2}v,w\rangle$; the spaces are mutually orthogonal and their algebraic sum is uniformly dense in $C(\mathbb S^2;\mathbb C)$. For smooth $f$, for every integer $m\ge1$ there is a constant $C_m(f)$ such that $\|P_\ell f\|_2\le C_m(f)(1+\ell)^{-m}$. For $g\in\mathcal H_\ell$,
$$\|g\|_\infty\le\sqrt{\frac{2\ell+1}{4\pi}}\,\|g\|_2.$$
For each integer $p\ge0$ there is $C_p$ independent of $\ell,g$ such that $\|g\|_{C^p(\mathbb S^2)}\le C_p(1+\ell)^{p+1/2}\|g\|_2$.
The angular Dirichlet form satisfies $-\langle\Delta_{\mathbb S^2}g,g\rangle=\ell(\ell+1)\|g\|_2^2$ for $g\in\mathcal H_\ell$.
For every continuous $f$, the ordered partial sums $\sum_{\ell=0}^N P_\ell f$ converge to $f$ in $L^2(\mathbb S^2)$.

pairs.actual_fact_text: [[lem-matching-nurbs-patch-traces-give-h1-conformity]] supplies global H1 membership for matching cell/patch values. [[lem-compactly-supported-h1-belongs-to-h-zero]] gives H1_0 membership for a compactly supported H1 function on any open set. [[def-bounded-piecewise-c-one-euclidean-domain]] and [[def-nurbs-patch-map-and-rational-spline-space]] specify the finite cell/facet presentation and the cellwise C1 NURBS maps.
pairs.supplier_statement_or_definition:
Under the $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ convention of [[def-bounded-c-one-domain-boundary-charts-and-outward-normal]], a finite piecewise $C^1$ presentation of a nonempty bounded open $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$, $n\ge2$, consists of compact faces $S_1,\ldots,S_q$ covering its boundary, each a compact Borel subset of a regular $C^1$ hypersurface patch, and a compact edge set $E\subset\partial\Omega$. Require $S_j\cap E$ to have surface measure zero in each face, using [[lem-surface-integral-is-independent-of-c-one-boundary-charts]]. E contains the boundaries of the faces relative to their patches and every overlap $S_i\cap S_j$, i different from j. At every point outside E the domain boundary is locally a single $C^1$ graph with Omega on one side. Each face carries this actual outward unit normal off E. Values assigned to the normal on E do not affect its integral.

For a specified finite gluing also list the open pieces with disjoint interiors, the shared faces, and their opposite outward normals. Require the pieces to cover the final domain up to their boundary faces, and the exposed faces to give its specified presentation. Internal faces are counted twice before cancellation, once from each side. The phrase piecewise smooth by itself supplies none of this data.

Proof1.2 uses the separate matching-trace supplier for global H1 membership, and Proof2.1 verifies null faces from C1 image maps of dimension d-1.
